title: How Zeroed works
subtitle: Paper mode only. How market data becomes a paper trade, and what must be proven before any deposit. Status at Sun 4 Oct 2026, 4:45 PM Melbourne.

lanes.title: Market data
lanes.blurb: Where the bot's information comes from. Free plans only, and every call is counted against a budget.

lanes.title: Bot on the server
lanes.blurb: The real worker's loop, paper mode only, top to bottom in the order things happen. Today the server still runs a stand-in; this loop starts there after the switch.

lanes.title: Your phone and alerts
lanes.blurb: A read-only view on your phone over a private link, plus alerts and a pause command in Telegram.

lanes.title: Proof before any deposit
lanes.blurb: Six proofs, all required, before the app asks for money. Left to right in the order they happen.

callouts.title: Paper only
callouts.text: The bot holds no signing key, and the worker has no way to send a transaction; any mode other than paper stops it at start. Each paper entry and exit is built as a real transaction and simulated on mainnet, never sent. Today nothing can enter, even on paper and in a practice run: the market-conditions check stays off, and checks H14 and H15 reject until their inputs are wired. After that, until research proves an edge, the cost check refuses every entry, so only a practice run trades on paper.

callouts.title: Exits never wait
callouts.text: Halts, your /pause and loss limits stop new entries only. Exits are always allowed, are served first from the call budget, and still run at 70% of the monthly credits. A sell is retried up to 5 times with fees rising from 0.00002 to 0.0005 SOL; after that the bot marks 'exit blocked' and keeps watching.

callouts.title: Loss limits
callouts.text: Each trade's stop sits at most 20% below the price after the buy. These stop new entries; open trades can still exit: daily loss of 7.5% of the bankroll (until midnight Melbourne), 2 losses in a row (2 h), 3 in a row (rest of the day), weekly loss of 20% (until the week ends and you review), 5 losses in 20 trades (until you review), kill switch at 70% of the peak (until you re-arm). If the heartbeat is over 90 s old, the watchdog alerts you, but it cannot sell: while the bot is down, an open trade has no working stop. Restart drills measure that gap.

callouts.title: What only you do
callouts.text: Fund the bot wallet and move money, switch paper to live, set the live risk limits, re-arm the kill switch, review a weekly-loss or 5-in-20 pause, clear a /pause at the server console (zeroed-resume), add or rotate API and wallet keys, approve paid services (such as the Helius full pull, at most US$99), approve personal data or data sent to a third party, and loosen any proof threshold. No code or agent does these. Keys live in GitHub secrets and in locked files on the server, never in the repo or in chat.

callouts.title: Blind to the future
callouts.text: The backtest runs the same engine core as live; only the data feed and clock change. Today it replays random picks only; the live checks and exit rules join it with the strategy study (in progress). A simulated clock releases each transaction in chain order, so later data is out of reach, and results are scored in a separate stage the engine never loads. Proof: a planted future marker must stay unseen, and 10 replays must give identical logs.
